independentFirstImpression.firstImpression: The first learning choice is immediately understandable: Familiar identities, Loup Tailored economy vs Restoring Humanity Ambushes. The page foregrounds learning goals and Runner win records. I can choose the familiar option without knowing advanced cards. It is not yet clear whether selecting a learning card configures the lobby; the cards have no visible action in the DOM controls. Initial pool remains Gateway although Vantage recommendations are at top.
independentFirstImpression.method: Actual shared preview; screenshot snapshot timed out. First guide DOM read still reported 1280px immediately after resize; await confirmed 390px before mobile findings.
independentFirstImpression.priorKnowledge: General software interaction and basic Netrunner vocabulary; no earlier panel reviews read.

steps: Read first pairing record and How to read the results section.

answers.runner28of54: 28 Runner wins out of 54 AI games implies 26 Corp wins, about 48% Corp wins. 52% is the Runner percentage; it is close in this sample, not proof of balance.
answers.sixGames: No reliable counter conclusion. Six-game records are preliminary; a single game moves the rate about 17 points. They suggest a matchup to try, and represent AI on both sides rather than human tournament strength.
answers.afterEdit: The benchmark does not carry to an edited deck. The guide says custom decks have not been benchmarked and exact bundled list names matter.

findings.title: Guide return does not preserve the user's browsing/setup intent
findings.evidence: Gateway→Vantage guide filter returned to Gateway lobby. Later configured Corp Jinteki vs AI Loup reopened guide; after changing its filter and returning, lobby used Runner Loup vs AI Jinteki. Both are observed browser outcomes; no source-level cause claimed.
findings.impact: A learner must reconstruct the pool and pairing, and can accidentally play the other side.
findings.improvement: Offer a keyboard-operable Use this pairing action carrying exact pool/list identifiers and selected human side. Preserve the invoking side on Back to lobby, and make clear whether explorer filters affect setup.
findings.acceptanceTest: Configure Corp Jinteki Ambushes vs AI Loup Tailored in Vantage. Open guide, browse another pool, return: human side and exact lists remain as configured. From Gateway guide, Use familiar pairing with Corp selected returns Vantage, human Jinteki, AI Loup without further selection.

findings.title: Section navigation links have small measured target height
findings.evidence: At 390px the three section links were 23.09px high; selects and checkbox label measured 44px high.
findings.impact: Narrow-screen section navigation may be less forgiving for touch input; actual touch accuracy was not tested.
findings.improvement: Give section and back links vertical padding for at least 44px target height while retaining wrapping.
findings.acceptanceTest: At 390×844 each section/back link has a target box at least 44px high; document width remains 390 with no horizontal overflow, and Tab/Enter still reaches and activates each link.

findings.title: The editor does not surface the benchmark consequence of a custom edit
findings.evidence: Guide explicitly says custom decks are unbenchmarked. After -1 Esca the editor showed draft changes and expansion audit note, without an equivalent benchmark reminder.
findings.impact: A learner returning from a guide recommendation may remember the pairing's percentage after changing the list.
findings.improvement: Show a concise 'Custom edits have not been benchmarked' note near draft changes, with a link to evidence reading help.
findings.acceptanceTest: Open a benchmarked bundled list, change a count, and verify the custom-edit benchmark note appears beside changes; restoring original counts clears the note, without implying AI certification.

strengths: Clear learning goals for first Vantage pairings.
Consistent Runner-perspective percentages and explicit Corp explanation.
Per-row sample counts and preliminary labels make mixed populations understandable.
Esca preview Escape correctly restored focus; editor retained selected pool, identity and draft validation.
